passage:
Dear Customer Support Team,

I am writing to formally express my disappointment regarding the service I received during my recent visit to your downtown branch on Monday afternoon. While I understand that employees can have demanding days, the behavior I encountered was unprofessional and fell well below reasonable customer service standards.

I visited the branch to resolve an issue with a billing error on my account. From the moment I approached the service desk, the representative appeared distracted and uninterested. Rather than greeting me or asking how they could help, they continued typing on their computer for several minutes without acknowledging my presence. When I explained the issue, their responses were short and dismissive, giving me the impression that my concern was an inconvenience.

What concerned me most was the lack of clear communication. The representative used technical terms without explanation and seemed irritated when I asked for clarification. At one point, they sighed audibly and stated that the issue was "probably my own mistake," without reviewing the account details thoroughly. This assumption made the interaction uncomfortable and unnecessarily confrontational.

Additionally, the tone of the conversation became increasingly unprofessional. When I requested to speak with a supervisor, the representative responded defensively and delayed the request. It was only after repeating myself that a supervisor was finally called, who then resolved the issue within minutes and confirmed that the billing error originated from the company's system.

While I appreciate that the supervisor handled the matter efficiently and courteously, the initial interaction left a lasting negative impression. Customers should feel respected, listened to, and supported—especially when dealing with financial concerns. Professionalism is not only about solving problems but also about how those problems are addressed.

I believe this situation could have been avoided with proper training in customer communication and conflict management. I hope this feedback will be taken seriously and used to improve service quality. I remain a loyal customer and would like to continue doing business with your company, but only if customer interactions are handled with professionalism and care.

Sincerely,
Nathan Cole
